title: Finite-coefficient smooth purity
statement:
Fix the purity conventions [def-pur-conventions] with their
explicit ingredients: the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$,
the prime $\ell\neq p$, the finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, the integer
$n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$; on the
small pro-etale site of a
$k$-scheme $T$, let $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ be the bounded
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] constructible
finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] for
$\Lambda=A$, with the
derived pullback,
tensor, and internal Hom, the
compact-support direct
image $Rf_!$, and the
constructible exceptional inverse image
$Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with the bounded-class
adjunction supplied by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], and let
$K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_T}\Lambda(m)$
be the coefficient twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] of degree
$m\in\mathbf Z$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
smooth – i.e. locally of finite
presentation, flat, with regular geometric fibers (equivalently a
formally smooth morphism of finite type) – separated morphism of
pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The
smooth purity map

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rf^!K
$$

of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $P=Lf^*K$, $U=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, and $V=\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$. The first factor of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is the specified canonical isomorphism $\rho:P(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes^L U$. This uses the twist convention $K(m)=K\otimes^L\Lambda(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; we take the shift reassociation from the explicitly stated first factor, not from a local choice of orientation.

source.place: Proof: three specified factors; realized by the explicit composite and inverse below

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] to the given smooth separated $f$ of pure relative dimension $d$, at the same finite coefficient level $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. The separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ in this item are in the domain of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], since $f$ is separated and of finite type. Thus the explicit scheme-domain hypotheses in the current cited statement hold. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\alpha:V\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. Consequently $t=\operatorname{id}_P\otimes^L\alpha^{-1}:P\otimes^L U\to P\otimes^L V$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $s=\operatorname{id}_P\otimes^L\alpha$: functoriality of derived tensor gives $s\circ t=\operatorname{id}$ and $t\circ s=\operatorname{id}$ from the two inverse identities for $\alpha$.

source.place: Proof: three specified factors; realized by the explicit composite and inverse below

proof.text: The tensor-formula clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], applied to this same $f$ and the given $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$, gives the canonical isomorphism $\beta:P\otimes^L V\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!K$. Both cited theorems use the purity conventions, hence the constructible pro-etale exceptional inverse image at this finite coefficient level; no additional site comparison or unrestricted ambient adjoint is used in this step.

source.place: Proof: three specified factors; realized by the explicit composite and inverse below

proof.text: By the definition [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], the morphism in the statement is exactly $\gamma_{f,K}=\beta\circ t\circ\rho$. Its inverse is $\rho^{-1}\circ s\circ\beta^{-1}$. Associativity and the inverse identities established above show that either ordered composite is the identity. Thus this specified smooth purity map is an isomorphism for every stated $K$.

source.place: Proof: three specified factors; realized by the explicit composite and inverse below

proof.text: For the vector-bundle model clause of the unit, let $Z$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $\pi:E\to Z$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Write $c_\pi:\Lambda_E(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi^!\Lambda_Z$ for the inverse of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Its normalization is determined by integration: [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] identifies the ordinary etale map with the adjoint of $t_\pi$, and [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] defines the constructible pro-etale adjoint by this etale/pro-etale transport. By [def-amb-vector-integration], on a trivializing open of $Z$ the trace is affine-space integration. More precisely, [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] specifies that integration as the counit of the ordered composite affine-line adjunctions, with the rank-one adjunction normalized by the restricted projective-line trace and rank zero by the identity adjunction. Its coefficient hypotheses hold: choose $N=\ell^r$ annihilating the finite ring $A_{E,n}$; $N$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme because $\ell\ne p$. The ordered affine-line comparison of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] has this same adjoint trace: [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] defines each factor as the adjoint of the restricted projective-line trace, and the counit of a composite $F_2F_1\dashv G_1G_2$ is $\epsilon_{2,K}\circ F_2(\epsilon_{1,G_2K})$. Iterating this formula shows that the adjoint of the ordered comparison is exactly the ordered trace specified in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]; the two maps therefore agree by injectivity of the adjunction bijection. Thus on a trivializing open $c_\pi$ is the affine-space comparison, with its specified normalization.

source.place: unit proof, second paragraph: agreement on the vector-bundle model; normalization on trivializing opens

proof.text: Choose a Zariski open cover $\{Z_i\}$ trivializing $E$, and let $E_i=E\times_Z Z_i$. The base-change compatibility clause of [cor-pur-dualizing-object-purity] applies to the canonical composite of the diagonal orientation with the tensor formula, which is exactly the map identified in Step 4. Apply this clause to each open base change $Z_i\hookrightarrow Z$; the schemes $Z_i,E_i$ remain separated and of finite type over $k$, and $\Lambda_{Z_i}$ has Tor amplitude zero. Consequently the restriction of $\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda_Z}$ to $E_i$ is the smooth purity map for $\mathbf A^d_{Z_i}\to Z_i$. By [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement], it is the ordered affine-space comparison, which is the restriction of $c_\pi$ by the preceding step and the base-change compatibility of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. To deduce global equality, form $h=c_\pi^{-1}\circ\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda_Z}$, an endomorphism of $\Lambda_E(d)[2d]$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the tensor-power definition of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $\Lambda_E(d)$ is a rank-one locally free sheaf in degree zero. Cancel the common shift. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $h$ then comes from a unique morphism of the degree-zero sheaf $\Lambda_E(d)$, hence from a section of its endomorphism sheaf. This endomorphism sheaf is canonically $\Lambda_E$: on any frame $e$ a linear endomorphism has the form $e\mapsto ae$, and replacing $e$ by $ue$ for a unit $u$ leaves $a$ unchanged. Thus the scalar descriptions glue independently of the frame. That section restricts to $1$ on every $E_i$, so the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives $h=1$ and $\gamma_{\pi,\Lambda_Z}=c_\pi$. Inverting gives precisely the vector-bundle model identification required by the unit, including rank zero.

source.place: unit proof, second paragraph: agreement on the vector-bundle model; descent of equality using endomorphisms of the Tate line

mathlib_searches.query: Smooth purity for finite torsion coefficients: exceptional inverse image equals smooth pullback with Tate twist and cohomological shift.

For a smooth separated morphism of schemes of pure relative dimension d and finite torsion coefficients invertible on the schemes, the canonical smooth purity map from derived pullback twisted by d and shifted by 2d to exceptional inverse image is an isomorphism.

mathlib_searches.query: Poincare duality for smooth morphisms: the extraordinary pullback on derived categories of constructible torsion sheaves is the ordinary inverse image tensored with the relative dualizing complex, which is the Tate twist shifted by twice the relative dimension.

proof.text:
The map was defined in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] as three
specified factors. The first is the twist reassociation of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The second is the inverse of
$\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ proved in
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] by the diagonal and deformation
argument. The third is the orientation-free tensor isomorphism of
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. Each factor is an
isomorphism, so their composite is an isomorphism for every stated
$K$. In particular this proof uses the proved diagonal
identification; applying $Rz^!$ at one section is not used as a
test of isomorphy for a complex on the entire affine space.
